verdict.rationale: skills.sh's core mechanism is exactly agent-oriented docs: SKILL.md files with name/description that agents load at startup (skills-cli-docs-3), a formal spec/validator (skills-cli-docs-4), and the ability to add skills from arbitrary URLs or direct SKILL.md/archive downloads (skills-cli-gh-23, skills-cli-gh-35). However, there is no evidence the product itself parses or points agents at the llms.txt convention specifically — the only llms.txt probe result is for github.com's own file, unrelated to skills.sh's own docs or workflow (skills-cli-probe-1), and skills.sh's own docs.md path 404s (skills-cli-probe-2). Missing for 10: explicit llms.txt ingestion/support, first-party documentation confirming llms.txt compatibility, and independent corroboration beyond the vendor's own repo/spec.
